title: Weber Kettle Steaks: ½" + 1"
imagePrompt: Four grilled beef steaks on a board: two thick ribeye-style steaks with rendered, crackling golden fat edges and two thinner strip-style steaks. Each has dark charcoal sear marks over a deep brown crust flecked with cracked black pepper. The thick steaks are sliced against the grain to show a rosy-pink medium-rare center with a thin gray-brown rim, juices beading on the cut faces and pooling slightly on the board.
subtitle: Two-zone charcoal on a Weber kettle for a mixed batch of pre-salted, room-temp steaks: thin ones seared hot and fast, thick ones seared then finished on the cool side.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: Steaks are already salted, peppered, dried, and at room temp. Do not salt again.
items: 2 thick steaks (~1"), ribeye/strip style with a fat edge
2 thin steaks (~½")
1 full chimney of charcoal, fully lit
1–2 tsp high-heat oil on a folded paper towel, for the grate
Flaky salt + butter (optional, to finish)
ingredients.callout: The whole game: all coals on one side. Thin steaks: hot side only, about 1½ min a side. Thick steaks: sear on the hot side, finish on the cool side, pull at 125°F.

body.html: Four steaks in two thicknesses on one fire. The trick is a two-zone fire and staggered timing: the 1" steaks go on first, and the ½" steaks go on when the thick ones move to the cool side. Everything comes off within a minute or two.

items: Mise en place: tools, thermometer, clean platter, oil rag, all next to the grill
Build the two-zone fire and preheat the grate 5 min
Sear the 1" steaks on the hot side, 2–3 min a side
Move them to the cool side, and drop the ½" steaks on the hot side
Pull everything by temp and feel, then rest 5 min

body.html: Thin steaks cook by the clock, thick steaks cook by the thermometer. A ½" steak goes from medium-rare to medium in about 30 seconds, so never walk away from it.

items: Sort the steaks into two groups: 1" and ½". Keep them apart on the tray.
Grab long tongs, an instant-read thermometer, a grill brush, and a clean platter (not the raw-meat tray).
Fold a paper towel into a pad and dab it with oil for the grate.
Optional: a pat of butter and flaky salt by the platter.

body.html: Don't re-salt. They're already seasoned. If a steak looks wet again, blot it right before it goes on.

slides.title: Two-Zone Fire
slides.checkboxLabel: Coals banked on one side, grate hot and oiled

items: Wait until the top coals in the chimney are ashed over gray and flames are licking out the top.
Dump all coals onto one half of the charcoal grate. Pile them in a slope. The other half stays empty: that's your cool side.
Bottom vent: fully open.
Set the cooking grate in place, lid on, top vent fully open, over the cool side. Preheat 5 min.
Brush the grate clean, then wipe the hot side with the oiled towel held in tongs.

body.html: Hand test: hold your palm 5" above the hot side. You should only last 1–2 seconds. Longer than that, give it a few more minutes.

items: Lay the 1" steaks on the hot side, lid off.
Don't touch for 2 min. Flip when it releases cleanly and has a dark crust.
Sear side 2 for 2–3 min.
Render the fat edge: stand each steak on its fat cap with tongs over the coals for 30–60 s until it's golden and crisp.

body.html: Flare-up? Slide the steak to the cool side for 10–15 s until the flames die down, then move it back. Don't squirt water on the coals.

slides.title: Finish 1" Cool / Sear ½" Hot
slides.checkboxLabel: Thin steaks seared, thick ones finishing

items: Move the 1" steaks to the cool side, right next to the coals.
Lay the ½" steaks on the hot side. Lid stays off: they cook fast.
½" side 1: 60–90 s → flip → side 2: 45–60 s → pull to the platter.
Pop the lid on for the 1" steaks. Start probing at 2 min.

body.html: Too thin to probe? Press the center: it should feel soft with a slight spring, like the base of your thumb when you touch thumb to middle finger. Pull early. They'll carry over.

slides.title: Pull + Rest
slides.checkboxLabel: All steaks pulled and rested 5 min

items: Probe the 1" steaks from the side into the center. Pull at 125°F for medium-rare.
Rest on the platter 5 min, uncovered. Optional: a pat of butter on top while they rest.
Slice across the grain, then a pinch of flaky salt on the cut faces.
Close all vents to kill the fire.

body.html: Carryover: thick steaks rise another 3–5°F while resting. Thin ones barely rise, so they can come off closer to target.

items: Steak sticks → not ready. Wait 15–30 s and it'll release.
Crust pale, center done → fire too cool. Next time, give the grate a longer preheat.
Crust dark, 1" center still raw → stay on the cool side, lid on, check every minute.
Constant flames → too much dripping fat. Work on the cool side and use the lid.
